en: -Cover effectiveness indicates what percentage of incoming projectiles will be stopped.\n- Projectiles will ignore cover that is 3x grid spaces in front of the shooter, This means that archers standing behind merlons will be protected but their arrows will not be stopped by the merlon.\n- Almost everything offers some cover, from bushes to torches. This means that for archers to have the best shot, they need a clear, unobstructed line of sight.

en: - All items like weapons, armour and apparel have a quality level. - Quality levels are: flimsy, sturdy, good, fine, superior and flawless. - Higher quality levels mean the item is more durable, and has better attributes, such as damage or range. Some items may have different modifiers depending on their quality. - Your settlers have a higher chance of producing better quality items if their skill in that field is higher. - When highly-skilled settlers are in a good mood, their chances of producing a flawless item will also increase slightly.

en:
<style=AlmParagraph>Outside & Inside Temperature
</style>- Outdoor temperature is shown in the top right corner of the screen next to the time.
- This temperature is the global outdoor temperature that is further modified by sunlight, shade, proximity to heat sources, etc. 
- Outdoor temperature depends on the season, time of day and active weather events such as cold snaps or heatwaves.
- You can inspect temperature using the temperature overlay on the upper left panel <sprite="temp_overlay_text_icon" index=t>. 
- To view indoor temperature, mouse over a room. Its temperature will be displayed replacing the outdoor temperature reading, in the top right corner. Alternatively, select the room to see this information.
- Indoor temperature depends on the outdoor temperature, and the room's insulation, as well as elements that have thermal output inside the room, like torches or a campfire.
<style=AlmParagraph>
Keeping cold
</style>If you want to have a colder room during the summertime, you can:
- build a room underground. 
- use material that has high insulation, such as clay.
- keep windows open and extinguish all heat sources inside that room.
- Note that windows that let sunlight in can also heat up the room
- Store ice blocks to further cool the area around them. 
<style=AlmParagraph>
Keeping warm
</style>If you want to have warm rooms during the wintertime, you can:
- place heat sources inside the rooms.
- close all windows to keep the warmth inside.

en:
<style=AlmParagraph><sprite="body_armor_icon" index=t> Armour rating
</style>- Armour rating further reduces the incoming damage after the armour penetration weapon attribute is taken into account. The higher the armour rating the better. 
- Armour rating reduces as the armour piece loses its HP.
<style=AlmParagraph>
<sprite="cover_icon" index=t> Cover amount
</style>- A shield's cover amount is the amount of incoming attacks the shield will absorb. Damage is fully absorbed by the shield but the shield takes the damage (multiplied by the weapon's armour damage).
- The final percentage of incoming blows absorbed is the shield cover amount + the opponent's evade chance attribute.

en:
<style=AlmParagraph><sprite="temperature_min_icon" index=t> Minimum comfortable temperature
</style>- Clothing can adjust the wearer's minimum comfortable temperature so that they are less affected by the cold. In the case of winter clothing, the wearer can withstand lower temperatures without negative effects. E.g.: A settler's minimum comfortable temperature is 3°C but winter clothing adds -20°C. The settler's effective minimum comfortable temperature is now -17°C.
<style=AlmParagraph>
<sprite="temperature_max_icon" index=t> Maximum comfortable temperature
</style>- Clothing can also adjust the wearer's maximum comfortable temperature. In the case of summer clothing, this means that they withstand higher temperatures without negative effects.

en: - An archer (or other settler with a ranged weapon equipped) placed at least one level higher than their target gets a bonus to precision, range and critical hit chance. The projectile's trail will be red when fired from higher ground.\n- If an archer is at least one level lower than their target, they will lose precision, range and critical hit chance. Projectiles fired from lower ground have a blue trail.

en:
- Modifiers vary attributes, priorities, mood and stats.
- Modifiers can be activated by consuming something or by equipping something
- E.g.: equipping heavy armour modifies a settler's movement and evade chance.
Each settler can activate differing modifiers, depending on their perks.
- E.g.: A settler with the Austere perk gets negative modifiers from a lavish meal , but positive effects from eating raw food.
- A list of active modifiers is found in the stats tab in the additional settler selection panel.
- A list of mood modifiers is found in the mood tab.

- Wounds are also a type of modifier, because they affect certain settler attributes. But they differ from regular modifiers because they can cause bleeding, and have varied effects depending on their severity.

en: Certain resources and items can decompose or rot Reasons for decomposition and rotting: - Being outdoors - Leaving your resources to get affected by the rain or snow will make them decompose faster. Place a roof over your stockpile to stop this from happening. - Temperature - Resources like food will decompose faster during the summer - Ground-type - Don’t leave your resources on the ground. Build floors underneath your stockpile zones to slow down decomposition.

Place a roof over your stockpile to stop this from happening. - Temperature - Resources like food will decompose faster during the summer - Ground-type - Don’t leave your resources on the ground. Build floors underneath your stockpile zones to slow down decomposition.

en: Some resources like curdling milk can ferment if the temperature is right. Resources that ferment will turn into new resources after the fermentation process is finished. Example: Curdling milk will turn into cheese.

en: - Each structure has a stability value. - This determines whether you can attach other structures to it. - When set on the ground, a structure has a stability value of 4. Each structure attached to it will have -1 stability the further away it is placed. - You cannot position a structure with a stability value of 0. - The vertical stability value remains unchanged. - To view the stability values around your current cursor position, turn the stability visualizer on. Beams - Place beams between two walls or terrain voxels. If one of these gets destroyed, this will also destroy the beam and everything resting on it. - A beam has a maximum range of 10 grid spaces. - The beam will inherit the lower stability value of the two walls/voxels it ties together. - Walls, windows, doors, roofs, merlons, and floors are the only things that you can place on beams.

- Click the pause icon or press [<style=Shortcut><input:GamePause></style>] to pause the game.
- You can give orders, place buildings, and draft settlers while the game is paused.

<style=Desc>TIP: This is especially useful if things get hectic.</style>

en:
- Prioritize each settler's tasks in the Jobs panel .
- Use <sprite="ctrl_left_click" index=t> to increase the priority of a job, and <sprite="ctrl_right_click" index=t> to decrease it.
- Settlers will always do the job with the highest priority first.
- If the job box is empty, the settler will never do that job.
- If numbers are equal, settlers will prioritise jobs from left to right.
- Box frames indicate the settler's skill level. Stars show their likes and dislikes.

<style=Desc>TIP: Settlers can fail jobs if their skill is low, so turning jobs off can be useful!</style>

en:
- You can unlock new technology in the research panel.
- Each research item requires books (chronicles, handbooks or theses).
- Research does not consume the books, but they must be kept safe.
- If your books are destroyed or lost, you will not be able to do new research.
- Research can be resumed once your previous book total is regained.

- Different quality outcomes will result in different mood and other buffs or debuff to the event's participants.

vi:
- Certain events can be triggered, like a <LinkAlmanac="Playertriggeredeventfeast">Feast</link> or a <LinkAlmanac="Playertriggeredeventsermon">Sermon</link>. 
- To launch these events, construct the corresponding room type, and select the structure within it which is the origin of the event. 
- Each event type has conditions, and will have varying levels of quality, depending on which conditions are met. 
- Different quality outcomes will result in different mood and other buffs or debuff to the event's participants. 
- Some events benefit from having a settler with a <LinkAlmanac="Roletypes">role</link> present.

en:
- You can give certain settlers special community roles. 
- These settlers have particular behaviours during role-appointed hours. 
- Certain criteria must be met to assign a role to a settler. 
- Roles help to increase your regional renown. 
- Some roles enhance events, improving their outcomes: e.g. a bard improves the quality of a <LinkAlmanac="Playertriggeredeventfeast">feast</link> .

en:
- Certain structures can be replaced with the same structure made from a different material. 
- Replacing structures such as walls, beams, and floors will not affect structural stability.
- Select a building and click the Replace Structure button in the lower-right corner. 
- Each replacement requires resources based on the selected material type. 
- Some replacement options may not be available if the required building material is missing. 
- Once a replacement is selected, a settler with a construction job will rebuild it. 
- Materials from the old structure will be returned to resource piles.
